steps: Order the data if finding the median
For frequency tables: add an fx column
For grouped data: use midpoints × frequency
State whether your answer is an estimate (grouped data = estimate)
method_card.title: Averages & Spread
method_card.content:
Mean = sum of values ÷ number of values. Median = middle value when ordered (for \(n\) values, position = \(\frac{n+1}{2}\)). Mode = most frequent value. Range = largest − smallest.

From a frequency table: Mean = \(\frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}\). For grouped data, use midpoints: mean = \(\frac{\sum f \times \text{midpoint}}{\sum f}\). Median class is found using \(\frac{n}{2}\). The modal class is the class with the highest frequency.

gold.display: Grouped data: 0-10(f=3), 10-20(f=7), 20-30(f=12), 30-40(f=8). Estimate the mean to 1 d.p.
The mean of a set of 10 numbers is 12. The mean of the first 6 is 10. Find the mean of the last 4.

misconceptions.message: Total of 10 = 120. Total of first 6 = 60. Total of last 4 = 60. Mean of last 4 = 60/4 = 15.

gold.display: A data set has mean 20 and range 15. Each value is multiplied by 3. What is the new range?

misconceptions.message: Multiplying all values by 3: new range = 3 × old range = 3 × 15 = 45.

gold.display: A data set has mean 20 and range 15. The value 5 is added to every number. What is the new mean?

misconceptions.message: Adding 5 to every value: new mean = 20 + 5 = 25. Range stays the same.

gold.display: Grouped data: 100-120(f=5), 120-140(f=10), 140-160(f=k), 160-180(f=5). The estimated mean is 140. Find \(k\).

misconceptions.message: Mode = most frequent. 5 appears 3 times. Mode = 5.

bronze.display: The mean of 5 numbers is 8. Find the total.
Seven students scored: 50, 60, 60, 65, 70, 75, 80. What is the mode?

silver.display: A frequency table shows: Score 1(f=3), 2(f=5), 3(f=8), 4(f=4). Find the mean.
A grouped frequency table: 0-10(f=4), 10-20(f=10), 20-30(f=6). Estimate the mean.
The mean of 4 numbers is 15. A fifth number is added and the mean becomes 18. What is the fifth number?

misconceptions.message: Original total = 4 × 15 = 60. New total = 5 × 18 = 90. Fifth number = 90 − 60 = 30.

silver.display: A grouped table: 0-20(f=5), 20-40(f=15), 40-60(f=10). Which is the modal class?

misconceptions.message: Modal class has the highest frequency. 20-40 has f=15.

silver.display: Find the median class for 30 values: 0-10(f=6), 10-20(f=12), 20-30(f=8), 30-40(f=4).

misconceptions.message: n/2 = 15th value. CF: 6, 18, 26, 30. 15th value falls in 10-20 (CF reaches 18).
Total = 20. Median position = (20+1)/2 = 10.5th. CF: 2, 7, 15, 18, 20. 10th and 11th values both in score 5 group. Median = 5.

silver.display: Data set: 2, 5, 5, 7, 8, 12. One more value is added and the median becomes 6. What could the new value be?

misconceptions.message: With 7 values, median = 4th value. Ordered with 6 inserted: 2, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12. Median = 6 ✓.
